literal: above there is no fixed command—what are the people to follow?
idiomatic: If the throne gives no fixed order, what can the people follow?"

literal: From now on those who fled and hid to escape hardship or wandered in other districts shall all return to their former dwellings; past crimes are not asked.
idiomatic: From now fugitives and wanderers shall return home without penalty for past crimes."

literal: When the people kill one another, governors and magistrates shall judge by law and private revenge is not permitted; [6] whoever dares revenge—execution extending to the clan;
idiomatic: Private killing is for magistrates to judge; [6] private revenge brings death to the whole clan;"

literal: neighboring households that aid are guilty as accomplices.
idiomatic: neighbors who help share the guilt."

literal: Provinces, commanderies, and districts must not send clerks and soldiers at will to trouble the people.
idiomatic: Provinces must not send soldiers to harass the people."

literal: If levies are issued, the district magistrate shall gather the village elders of three districts to assess property and fix the levy, gathering more from the many to aid the few, mixing nine grades—rich must not press the poor nor strong harm the weak.
idiomatic: When levies come, elders shall fix fair assessments by wealth, mixing grades so the rich cannot crush the poor."

literal: The governor shall review ability, verify achievement, and report in order to the province.
idiomatic: Governors shall review work and report to the province."

literal: The inspector shall clearly assess excellence and baseness, suppress corrupt clerks, advance the upright, and at year's end present accounts to the capital.
idiomatic: Inspectors shall rank officials, remove the corrupt, promote the good, and report yearly."

literal: Governors bear the charge of governing the people; they should proclaim favor, obey the statutes, share the state's worry, keep the straight way and correct the person, and dwell gravely in office—is this not good?"
idiomatic: Governors must teach kindness, obey law, share the state's cares, and keep upright office."

literal: " On guimao envoys were sent with the great offering to sacrifice at the Northern Peak.
idiomatic: On guimao envoys sacrificed at the Northern Peak with the great offering."

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jiayin: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the second year, first month of spring, on jiayin the court returned to the capital.

literal: Second month, day wuzi: Feng Wentong sent envoys with tribute, asking to send an attendant son; the Emperor did not permit.
idiomatic: On wuzi of the second month Wentong asked to send his heir; the emperor refused.

literal: On renchen more than ten envoys were sent to Gaoli and the eastern Yi states with proclamations.
idiomatic: On renchen more than ten envoys were sent to Gaoli and the eastern Yi.

literal: Third month, day bingchen: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On bingchen of the third month Liu Yilong sent tribute.

literal: On xinwei General Who Pacifies the East E Qing and General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi led ten thousand elite horse against Feng Wentong; Governor of Ping province Yuan Ying also led the Liaoxi generals to join them.
idiomatic: On xinwei E Qing and Gu Bi led ten thousand horse against Wentong; Yuan Ying of Ping brought Liaoxi troops to meet them.

literal: [7] Wentong was pressed hard and begged aid from Gaoli; Gaoli sent its great general Ge Manlu with twenty thousand foot and horse to welcome Wentong.
idiomatic: [7] Wentong, hard pressed, begged Gaoli; Gaoli sent Ge Manlu with twenty thousand men to receive him.

literal: On jiaxu, by appointment
idiomatic: On jiaxu, by appointment

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: garrison Hulao.
idiomatic: to garrison Hulao.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiashen: the imperial sons Xiao'er and Miao'er both died.
idiomatic: On jiashen of the fourth month of summer Princes Xiao'er and Miao'er died.

literal: Fifth month, day yimao: Feng Wentong fled to Gaoli.
idiomatic: On yimao of the fifth month Wentong fled to Gaoli.

literal: On wuwu an edict that Attendant Cadet Feng Bo was envoy to Gaoli to demand Wentong be sent.
idiomatic: On wuwu he sent Feng Bo to Gaoli to demand Wentong.

literal: On dingmao traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On dingmao he went to Hexi.

literal: When Helian Ding went west, Yang Nachang seized Shanggui by stealth.
idiomatic: After Helian Ding went west, Yang Nachang seized Shanggui.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengxu: an edict that General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, and others were to direct the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against him.
idiomatic: On gengxu of the seventh month of autumn he ordered Prince Pi of Leping against Shanggui.

literal: An edict that Attendant Cadet, Viscount of Guangping You Ya, and others were envoys to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered You Ya, Attendant Cadet and Viscount of Guangping, to Liu Yilong.

literal: Eighth month, day dinghai: six envoys were sent to the Western Regions.
idiomatic: On dinghai of the eighth month six envoys went to the Western Regions.

literal: The Emperor conducted a hunt in Hexi.
idiomatic: The emperor hunted in Hexi.

literal: An edict that Duke of Guangping Zhang Li was to mobilize twelve thousand men from seven commanderies of Ding province to open the Shaqüan road.
idiomatic: He ordered Zhang Li to raise twelve thousand men from seven Ding commands to open the Shaqüan road.

literal: On jiachen the Gaoche state sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On jiachen the Gaoche sent tribute.

literal: Ninth month, day gengxu: General of Agile Cavalry Prince of Leping Pi and the others reached Lüeyang; Nachang received the edict and took charge of Shanggui's defense.
idiomatic: On gengxu of the ninth month Pi reached Lüeyang; Nachang obeyed and held Shanggui.

literal: Gaoli did not send Wentong but sent envoys with a memorial, saying they would submit to royal transformation together with Wentong.
idiomatic: Gaoli refused to send Wentong but offered to submit with him.

literal: The Emperor, because Gaoli disobeyed the edict, deliberated striking them.
idiomatic: The emperor, angered that Gaoli defied the order, considered an attack.

literal: He accepted Prince of Leping Pi's plan and stopped.
idiomatic: He took Prince Pi's counsel and desisted.

literal: Winter, eleventh month, day jiyou: traveled to Yuyang, drove wild horses in Yunzhong, and established the Wild Horse Park.
idiomatic: On jiyou of the eleventh month of winter he went to Yuyang, rounded up wild horses at Yunzhong, and founded the Wild Horse Park.

literal: Intercalary month, day renzi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On renzi of the intercalary month the court returned to the capital.

literal: On yichou Prince of Yingchuan Ti was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wuchang.
idiomatic: On yichou Prince Ti of Yingchuan became Prince of Wuchang.

literal: Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, sent tribute.

literal: That year Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun died.
idiomatic: That year Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun died.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day guiwei: General Who Conquers the East, Prince of Zhongshan Zuan, died.
idiomatic: On guiwei of the third year, first month of spring, Prince Zuan of Zhongshan died.

literal: On wuzi Grand Tutor, Prince of Beiping Changsun Song, died.
idiomatic: On wuzi Changsun Song, Grand Tutor and Prince of Beiping, died.

literal: On yisi General Who Guards the South, Prince of Danyang Shusun Jian, died.
idiomatic: On yisi Shusun Jian, Prince of Danyang, died.

literal: Second month, day yimao: traveled to You province, comforted the old and orphaned, and inquired into the people's hardships;
idiomatic: On yimao of the second month he went to You, comforted the aged and orphans, and asked after the people's hardships;

literal: returned and traveled to Shanggu, then reached Dai.
idiomatic: then went to Shanggu and on to Dai.

literal: Along the route half the field tax was remitted.
idiomatic: Half the land tax along the route was remitted.

literal: Gaoli and the Khitan state each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Gaoli and the Khitan sent tribute.

literal: Third month, day dingchou: Prince of Nanping Hun was made General Who Guards the East, equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and garrisoned Helong.
idiomatic: On dingchou Prince Hun of Nanping was made commander of the east and garrisoned Helong.

literal: On jimao the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On jimao the court returned to the capital.

literal: On guisi Kucha, Yueban, Yanqi, Cheshi, Sogdiana, Shule, Wusun, Khotan, and Shanshan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On guisi Kucha, Yueban, Yanqi, Cheshi, Sogdiana, Shule, Wusun, Khotan, and Shanshan sent tribute.

literal: On dingyou Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On dingyou Liu Yilong sent tribute.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day jichou: an edict said: "At present the rebel bandits are destroyed and the realm gradually grows calm.
idiomatic: On jichou of the fifth month of summer an edict said: "Rebels are gone and the realm grows calm."

literal: In recent years We have repeatedly ordered the offices to proclaim favor and give the people rest.
idiomatic: We have often ordered favor and rest for the people."

literal: Yet officials within and without and governors, magistrates, and chiefs cannot diligently attend their charge, investigate the unlawful, abandon public duty for private ends, conceal one another, trade goods for office, and government rests on the perfunctory.
idiomatic: Yet officials and magistrates neglect duty, hide wrongdoing, trade bribes for office, and govern carelessly."

literal: When law is not used, the fault begins above; let officers and people throughout the realm be permitted to report governors and magistrates who do not follow the law.
idiomatic: Where law fails, the fault is from the top; let anyone report magistrates who break the law."

literal: " On bingshen traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: On bingshen he went to Yunzhong."

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day wuzi: Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, and Minister of Works, Prince of Shangdang Changsun Daosheng, were sent to campaign against the remnant band of Mountain Hu Bai Long in Xihe and destroy them.
idiomatic: On wuzi of the seventh month of autumn Prince Jian and Changsun Daosheng destroyed Bai Long's remnant in Xihe.

literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On jiachen of the eighth month he went to Hexi.

literal: Ninth month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On jiashen of the ninth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: On dingyou envoys were sent to invest Murong Muliyan, younger brother of Western Qin King Mugui, as General Who Guards the West, equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and re-enfeoff him as King of Xiping.
idiomatic: On dingyou envoys invested Muliyan as King of Xiping.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: On guimao of the tenth month of winter he went to Yunzhong.

literal: Eleventh month, day renshen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On renshen of the eleventh month the court returned to the capital.

literal: On jiashen Poluo and Zheshe states each sent envoys with tribute, presenting blood-sweating horses.
idiomatic: On jiashen Poluo and Zheshe sent tribute, including blood-sweating horses.

literal: That year the heir of Juqu Mujian, King of Hexi, Feng Tan, came to court.
idiomatic: That year Feng Tan, heir of Juqu Mujian, came to court.

literal: Year 4, spring, third month, day gengchen: the younger brother of the King of Shanshan, Su Yanqi, came to court.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, third month of spring, on gengchen Su Yanqi, brother of the King of Shanshan, came to court.

literal: On guiwei monks under fifty years of age were dismissed.
idiomatic: On guiwei monks under fifty were dismissed from orders.

literal: Prince of Jiangyang Gen died.
idiomatic: Prince Gen of Jiangyang died.

literal: That month Gaoli killed Feng Wentong.
idiomatic: That month Gaoli killed Feng Wentong.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day wuyin: general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On wuyin of the fifth month of summer he granted amnesty to the empire.

literal: On bingshen traveled to Wuyuan.
idiomatic: On bingshen he went to Wuyuan.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renwu: the imperial carriage campaigned north.
idiomatic: On renwu of the seventh month of autumn the court marched north.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the treatise on the Rouran.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: a great feast for the Six Armies.
idiomatic: On yichou of the tenth month of winter he feasted the Six Armies.

literal: Twelfth month, day dingsi: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
idiomatic: On dingsi of the twelfth month the court returned from the north.

literal: Tan and others of Ba Springs in Shangluo led one another inward in submission.
idiomatic: Tan and others of Ba Springs in Shangluo submitted together.

literal: An edict that Concurrent Attendant Cadet Gao Ya was envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered Gao Ya, Concurrent Attendant Cadet, to Liu Yilong.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Year 5, spring, first month, day gengyin: traveled to Ding province.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, first month of spring, on gengyin he went to Ding.

literal: Third month, day dingmao: an edict that General of the Guard, Prince of Le'an Fan, was to send Governor of Yongzhou Ge Na to take Shangluo; Liu Yilong's Administrator of Shangluo Tan Changsheng abandoned the commandery and fled.
idiomatic: On dingmao he ordered Fan to send Ge Na against Shangluo; Tan Changsheng fled.

literal: On xinwei the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On xinwei the court returned to the capital.

literal: On gengyin the former heir of the late King of Southern Qin, Yang Baozong, was made General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Qinzhou, King of Wudu, and garrisoned Shanggui.
idiomatic: On gengyin Yang Baozong, former heir of Southern Qin, was made King of Wudu and garrisoned Shanggui.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingyou: Shanshan, Kucha, Shule, and Yanqi each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On dingyou of the fourth month of summer Shanshan, Kucha, Shule, and Yanqi sent tribute.

literal: Fifth month, day dingchou: troops were drilled at the western suburb.
idiomatic: On dingchou of the fifth month the army was drilled at the western suburb.

literal: On guiwei Zheyi state presented blood-sweating horses.
idiomatic: On guiwei Zheyi presented blood-sweating horses.

literal: Sixth month, day jiachen: the imperial carriage campaigned west against Juqu Mujian; Palace Attendant, Prince of Yidu Mu Shou assisted the crown prince in deciding capital affairs;
idiomatic: On jiachen of the sixth month the court marched west against Juqu Mujian; Mu Shou, Prince of Yidu, assisted the crown prince at the capital;

literal: Grand General, Prince of Changle Ji Jing, and General Who Assists the State, Prince of Jianning Chong, with twenty thousand men encamped in the southern desert against the Rouran.
idiomatic: Ji Jing of Changle and Prince Chong of Jianning with twenty thousand camped south against the Rouran.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jisi: the imperial carriage reached Shang commandery Shuguo city, held a great feast for the ministers, and practiced martial archery on horseback.
idiomatic: On jisi of the seventh month of autumn the court reached Shuguo in Shang, feasted the ministers, and held mounted archery.

literal: On renwu the baggage train was left behind and the armies were divided: Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, and Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Julu Liu Jie directed the armies, [10] advancing with Prince of Changshan Su by two routes as vanguard;
idiomatic: On renwu baggage was left behind; Prince Jian and Liu Jie led the armies, [10] advancing with Prince Su of Changshan in two columns as vanguard;

literal: General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, and Grand Preceptor, Prince of Yangping Du Chao directed the armies of Pingliang and Fucheng as rear guard.
idiomatic: Prince Pi of Leping and Du Chao of Yangping followed with the Pingliang and Fucheng forces.

literal: Eighth month, day jiawu: Prince of Yongchang Jian captured more than two hundred thousand of Mujian's cattle, horses, and livestock.
idiomatic: On jiawu of the eighth month Prince Jian took more than two hundred thousand head from Mujian.

literal: Mujian sent his younger brother Donglai with more than ten thousand men to resist south of the city; seeing the dust they withdrew.
idiomatic: Mujian's brother Donglai met them south of the city with ten thousand men and fled at the dust.

literal: On bingshen the imperial carriage reached Guzang; Mujian's nephew Zuyu came over the wall in surrender; the army was then divided to besiege.
idiomatic: On bingshen the court reached Guzang; Zuyu surrendered over the wall and the army besieged.

literal: Ninth month, day bingxu: Mujian's nephew Wannian led his followers in surrender.
idiomatic: On bingxu of the ninth month Wannian surrendered with his men.

literal: That day Mujian, with five thousand civil and military followers, came bound to the camp gate; the Emperor released his bonds and treated him with the ceremony due a frontier prince.
idiomatic: That day Mujian came bound with five thousand followers; the emperor freed him and treated him as a vassal king.

literal: More than two hundred thousand households within the city and treasures in the storehouses beyond counting were taken.
idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand households and uncounted treasure were taken.

literal: Duke of Zhangye Tufa Baozhou was advanced to prince; Dragon-Agile General Mu Pi and General Who Pacifies the Distance Yuan He divided to reduce the commanderies; mixed peoples who submitted also numbered several hundred thousand.
idiomatic: Baozhou of Zhangye was made prince; Mu Pi and Yuan He reduced the districts; hundreds of thousands more submitted.

literal: Mujian's younger brother Yide, Administrator of Zhangye, burned the storehouses and fled west to Jiuquan;
idiomatic: Yide, Zhangye governor and Mujian's brother, burned the stores and fled to Jiuquan;

literal: Anzhou, Administrator of Ledu, fled south to Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: Anzhou of Ledu fled south to Tuyuhun.

literal: General Who Guards the South Xi Juan was sent against Zhangye and then reached Jiuquan; Mujian's younger brother Wuwei, Administrator of Jiuquan, and Yide again fled to Jinchang.
idiomatic: Xi Juan took Zhangye and reached Jiuquan; Wuwei and Yide fled again to Jinchang.

literal: Acting Prince of Yiyang Yuan Jie was left to guard Jiuquan.
idiomatic: Yuan Jie, Acting Prince of Yiyang, was left to hold Jiuquan.
